title: A warmer surface in air
hook: Change temperature difference and predict convective heat rate.
misconception: convective heat rate stays fixed when temperature difference doubles.
objective: Apply Q̇ = hAΔT to compare convective heat rate when temperature difference changes, under the stated assumptions.

claims.text: With fixed convection coefficient and surface area, Q̇ = hAΔT. When temperature difference doubles, convective heat rate becomes 2 times its original value.
claims.source: Idealized model Q̇ = hAΔT; scaling exponent 1. Physics and assumptions await independent review.

recall.question: Consider fixed convection coefficient and surface area, with a nonzero initial result. If temperature difference triples from a positive value, what is the multiplier on convective heat rate?
recall.why: Apply Q̇ = hAΔT under the same assumptions: the multiplier is 3.
